sources.note: No linguistic hit for 'Khamla' at all (only a Nagpur locality, a Lao/Thai given name, an elephant). CrossRef returns nothing relevant for Gowli or Khamla. No sociolinguistic survey, grammar, phonology or wordlist of Gowli/Khamla surfaced.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds). 2013. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 17th ed., entry 'Gowli' [gok] (Wayback Machine capture 2013-04-25)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Establishes identity: 'Dialects Khamla, Lingaayat, Nand, Ranya. Nand subdialects have 93% or higher intelligibility with Khamla dialect. Dialect used in Madhya Pradesh appears more similar to Marathi [mar] (Southern zone) than to Hindi [hin] (Central zone). Lexical similarity: 84%-92% between the Ranya and Nand dialects.' Population 35,000 (IMA 1997); 'Speakers belong to Gowli caste... Surrounded by Korku [kfq].' Classification Indo-Aryan, Central zone, Western Hindi, Unclassified.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group, Part I: Specimens of Western Hindi and Panjabi. Calcutta: Superintendent Government Printing. pp. 550, 554-555 ('Gaoli, Raghobansi, and Kirari')
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 554: 'GAOLI, RAGHOBANSI, and KIRARI. These are the dialects of the castes implied by their names. They are all reported from Chhindwara... Gaoli 16,093... The dialects spoken by them were originally classed in the Rough List of Languages spoken in Chhindwara District, as forms of Malwi. As a matter of fact, they in no way differ from the ordinary broken Bundeli of the district.' p. 555 gives a Bundeli (Gaoli) specimen of the Parable with a note on the agentive -ne with intransitive verbs; no prosody.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3. Languoid 'Gowli' gowl1241 [gok] (Bookkeeping), editors' spurious-entry comment
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States the parent entry is spurious: Ethnologue's Gowli [gok] and Gowlan [goj] 'can only match one and the same caste, i.e., the Gowāri (also Gaoli/Gowli/Gowlan) caste (Russell & Hiralal 1916), so at least one of the entries is spurious, and, on purely linguistic grounds, both are spurious, since the Gowli do not have a language that is mutually unintelligible with all surrounding languages (Grierson 1916 [LSI IX.1]: 554-555, Russell & Hiralal 1916).' Glottolog reference list for gowl1241 is empty.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank (eds). Glottolog 5.3. Languoid 'Khamla' kham1280 (Bookkeeping)
sources.note: Nothing. Page says: 'This entry has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes. Either the entry has been replaced with one or more more accurate entries or it has been retired because it was based on a misunderstanding to begin with.' Only alternative name: multitree 'Khamla'. No references, no coordinates, no ISO code.
Nothing. Repeats Ethnologue dialect list 'Khamla, Lingaayat, Nand, Ranya'; reports Bible portions and a New Testament 2017-2023 for Gowli, but names no linguistic description.

Nothing. Shows where kham1280 comes from: node ID gok_kha 'Khamla', Node_Type Dialect, child of gok 'Gowli' (alt. name Nand; 'India. Madhya Pradesh; Maharashtra, Amravati District.'), in trees 14596 (Ethnologue 15, Gordon 2005), 19655 (composite) and 21328 (Ethnologue 16, Lewis 2009). No source beyond Ethnologue.
